source.title: Black Boxes, White Noise: Similarity Detection for Neural Functions

record.tranche_reason: The study measures functional similarity between classifier outputs, not alignment or distance geometry of learned representations. It does not test convergence with model scale, cross-modal alignment, or the other listed representation claims.
record.gate_note: The experiments compare classifier output predictions on random inputs using CCA, Spearman correlation, and overlap. These are results about functional clone detection, not representational convergence. Related-work citations about representation similarity are not study results.
record.test_reason: The study tests whether random inputs and three output-level metrics (CCA, Spearman, overlap) can detect functionally similar Keras classifiers for clone detection. It measures agreement between classifier outputs, not the alignment of learned representations or features. Its results bear on no claim version. It mentions representation-similarity work, including the Convergent Learning original, only in related work, to contrast its own functional approach.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is essentially correct. The authors conclude that random inputs can replace canonical inputs for detecting functionally similar DNN classifiers, with Spearman the best overall metric. Overlap with balanced (BRINC) inputs helps when architectures differ substantially. Detection can fail for substantially different architectures or low-accuracy models.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares classifier output behavior on random inputs rather than comparing learned representation geometry on canonical inputs. It uses output CCA, output-wise Spearman correlation, and label overlap; it does not test the original representation-convergence methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Functional-similarity detection varies with metric, input construction (unconstrained versus balanced random inputs for overlap), and model properties. The text reports weak performance of CCA and Spearman for the substantially different CNN architecture case; it also describes effects from learning rate and accuracy in the D14 sensitivity analysis.

fits_no_version.finding: In D14, two separately trained identical MLPs (MN Ver1/Ver2) had the highest output similarity on random inputs. CNNs versus the MLP reference fell in the dissimilar region for CCA and Spearman, despite similar MNIST accuracy (Section 5, Fig. 7).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Output-level functional agreement on random (out-of-distribution) inputs is high across training seeds but low across substantially different architectures solving the same task.

fits_no_version.finding: Clone-detection accuracy on 1,037 comparisons was 83% for CCA, 94% for Spearman and 76% for overlap. CCA and Spearman found no true positives against a CNN reference.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Random-input functional-similarity detection of classifiers depends on metric and architecture difference.

record.peer_reviewed: The Art, Science, and Engineering of Programming
record.problems: The study is limited to single-label classifiers with compatible input shapes and the same number and ordering of output classes. The reported comparison uses mean aggregation across output classes. Some sensitivity results are presented in figures, and no statistical uncertainty estimates are stated for the aggregate performance figures.
record.rows_left_out: No other claim-related representation-convergence results were reported. Findings about specific D14 training settings and model properties are summarized in the authors' conclusion and method-sensitivity field rather than extracted as individual functional-similarity rows.

untested.parts: All: no representations compared across model scale or capability.
All: no vision-language models or paired data.
All: separately trained instances (MN Ver1/Ver2) are compared only on output similarity, not on features or subspaces.
All: no mapping, stitching or relative representations.
All: no interpretable features or circuits.
All: metric dependence is shown for output-level clone detection, not for representational convergence measures.

record.verdict_notes: The relation is changed from 'discusses' to 'cites_only'. Representation-similarity literature appears only in related work and the metric motivation. The MN Ver1/Ver2 and CNN results superficially resemble seed and architecture convergence, but they are output agreements on white-noise inputs used to evaluate a clone detector. They are recorded under fits_no_version rather than linked to V3 or V1.

versions.untested_parts: Convergence of representations across model sizes, capabilities, architectures, objectives, and data.
Vision-language alignment on paired images and captions as model performance changes.
Shared features or subspaces across independently initialized networks.
Mapping or stitching representations, relative representations, or alignment without paired data.
Recurrence of interpretable features or circuits across models.
The dependence of representational convergence on similarity metrics, settings, or input distributions.
Whether representational alignment is incomplete or explained by shared data or objectives.

rows.subject: Two similar digit-recognition models (Model1 and Model2; names as given in Appendix A)
rows.operation_detail: Compared overlap similarity using unbalanced and balanced random inputs.

conditions.value: unbalanced random inputs versus BRINC balanced inputs

rows.baseline: With unbalanced inputs, predictions were scattered and reached approximately 40% for both similar and dissimilar candidates in one case.
rows.value: With balanced inputs, values formed clusters and the authors state a threshold could separate similar models without false positives; the similar models were above approximately 20%.
rows.note: Qualitative result about functional-similarity detection and input construction, not representational convergence.
rows.check: About input balancing for the overlap metric. This is method design, not convergence.

rows.subject: MN Ver1 and other D14 models (aggregate sensitivity result)
rows.operation_detail: Repeated similarity measurements over 10 separately generated random input datasets.

conditions.value: 10 separately generated datasets; unconstrained inputs for CCA and Spearman, BRINC inputs for overlap

rows.measure: Variation in functional-similarity scores across input generations
rows.value: The text describes variation as negligible for CCA and Spearman; overlap showed some variability within relatively narrow bands.
rows.note: The text gives this qualitative description; the plot contains the individual distributions.
rows.check: Stability of output-similarity scores across random input draws. This is a stability measure of the method, not of representations.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
